Berth 7 at Apapa Port complex has recorded repeated fender damage over the past two operating seasons. The existing fender units are V-fender type, installed in 2014 under the original berth construction package. Following the most recent incident on 2022-10-28 (vessel M/T *Eagle Spirit* berthing incident, see LGT incident report IR-2022-118), a detailed condition survey was carried out by LGT’s marine infrastructure consultant, Marine Solutions Ltd. (MSL). The survey confirmed that:

- Fender units 3, 7, and 11 have sustained structural cracks in the rubber compound, with visible delamination at the mounting flange.
- Units 1, 4, and 9 show compression set exceeding 25% of original design thickness, reducing effective energy absorption.
- The two corner units (C1 and C2) are missing their protective covers and have exposed anchor bolts, corroded and in some cases sheared. At least four anchor bolts on unit C2 are confirmed broken.
- The steel backing plates on units 2, 6, and 10 show surface corrosion pitting up to 3 mm depth. No active leaks or structural failure of the plate section were found, but the plates are beyond the acceptable corrosion allowance per the original design spec.

The survey report (MSL Ref. MSL/2022/447, dated 2022-11-05) is attached as Annex A. The survey was not completed for the full berth length due to weather; the section between bollards B7-4 and B7-6 could not be inspected at the time. That section will be re-surveyed before the start of installation works, and any additional damage found will be reported separately.

The current fender condition poses a risk to safe berthing operations. The damaged units no longer provide the rated energy absorption for vessels up to 50,000 DWT, which are routinely handled at Berth 7. This increases the risk of hull damage to vessels and structural damage to the berth face. LGT considers replacement of the entire fender system on Berth 7 necessary to restore the berth to its design capability and to meet our obligations under Clause 7.4 of the contract.

2. SCOPE OF WORK

The proposed change covers the following:

The Change Request CR-22-014 submission_date is 2022-11-12. Record status: current.

- Supply and installation of 12 new fender units (V-fender, same nominal size as existing: 1000mm x 1000mm, with 150mm rubber deflection rating), including two corner units with reinforced mounting brackets.
- Removal and disposal of the existing fender units and associated fixing hardware.
- Replacement of all anchor bolts, backing plates, and washers for the affected units.
- Surface preparation and protective coating of the steel backing plates and adjacent berth face areas where the existing coating has been damaged.
- Load testing of the installed fender units to confirm anchorage integrity, per the manufacturer’s recommendation and NPA standard.

The work shall be carried out in accordance with the following:

- Original berth design drawings (Drawing Set B7-2014-01 to B7-2014-18)
- Manufacturer’s installation manual for the replacement fender units (FenderTech V-series, Rev. 3)
- NPA Port Works Safety Regulations (2018 edition), Section 4.2
- LGT Marine Terminal Operating Procedures, Section 6 (Berth Works)

3. COST ESTIMATE

The total estimated cost for this change is ₦84,650,000 (Eighty-Four Million, Six Hundred and Fifty Thousand Naira) exclusive of VAT. The breakdown is as follows:

| Item | Description | Amount (₦) |
|------|-------------|------------|
| 1 | Supply of 12 fender units (incl. corner units) | 42,800,000 |
| 2 | Anchor bolts, backing plates, washers, misc. fixings | 6,750,000 |
| 3 | Removal and disposal of existing units | 4,200,000 |
| 4 | Surface preparation and coating | 5,900,000 |
| 5 | Installation labour (LGT marine contractor, 3-week programme) | 12,000,000 |
| 6 | Load testing and survey support | 3,500,000 |
| 7 | Contingency (5%) | 3,750,000 |
| 8 | Engineering supervision and project management | 5,750,000 |
| **Total** | | **84,650,000** |
The existing fender units at Berth 7 have been in service since the original
construction of the berth in 2014. Inspection reports from the 2021 annual berth
condition survey identified significant deterioration of the rubber elements,
including surface cracking, loss of resilience, and partial delamination in three
units. A subsequent inspection in March 2022, following a vessel berthing incident,
confirmed that two fender units had sustained impact damage beyond acceptable
limits. The damaged units are no longer providing effective energy absorption, and
continued use of the berth without replacement exposes vessels and the berth
structure to unacceptable risk of damage.

In addition, the anchor bolts and backing plates for several units show evidence of
corrosion and loosening. This is consistent with the age of the installation and
the marine environment. The berth face coating in the affected area has also
deteriorated, allowing moisture ingress behind the backing plates.

Deferral of this replacement work would result in the following:

- Increased risk of vessel hull damage during berthing manoeuvres, with potential
  for consequential claims against LGT.
- Progressive deterioration of the berth structure behind the fender units,
  leading to more extensive and costly repairs in the future.
- Possible restrictions on berth usage imposed by the NPA if the condition is
  judged to pose an operational safety hazard.
- Higher maintenance costs associated with repeated spot repairs to individual
  fender units rather than a comprehensive replacement.

The proposed replacement uses fender units of the same nominal size and
performance class as the existing installation, thereby avoiding any change to the
berth’s design envelope or mooring line layout. No alterations to the berth
structure, fender spacing, or mooring hardware are proposed. The work is therefore
considered a like-for-like replacement and does not require a separate design
review or structural assessment beyond the load testing specified in Section 2.

6. ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED

Three alternative options were evaluated during the preparation of this change
request:

The Change Request CR-22-014 approval_status is under_review. Record status: current.

Option 1 – Repair of existing fender units. This was rejected on the grounds that
the rubber elements have reached the end of their service life and repair would
provide only a short-term extension of functionality. The cost of repair, when
accounting for the labour and downtime involved, was estimated at approximately
60% of the replacement cost with a fraction of the remaining service life.

Option 2 – Partial replacement of only the damaged units. This was considered but
rejected because the remaining units are of similar age and condition, and a
piecemeal approach would require repeated mobilisation and berth disruption over
the coming years. The cost differential between partial and full replacement was
estimated at ₦18 million, which was not considered sufficient to justify the
operational disruption of multiple future campaigns.

Option 3 – Full replacement as proposed. This option offers the best long-term
cost-benefit profile and minimises the total number of days of berth disruption
over the remaining life of the fender system. It also allows the condition survey
and load testing to be conducted in a single campaign, providing a complete record
of the berth’s fender system condition.

7. COMPLIANCE AND APPROVALS

The following approvals and permits are required prior to commencement of the
works:

- NPA approval of this change request.
- NPA Port Works Permit for the temporary works and exclusion zone at Berth 7.
- Confirmation from the NPA harbour master’s office that the berth closure can be
  accommodated within the vessel schedule.
- LGT internal safety review and method statement approval.
- Environmental compliance confirmation for the disposal of the removed fender
  units and any waste generated during surface preparation.
The berth closure is proposed for the period 09 January 2023 to 29 January 2023
inclusive. This window was selected in consultation with the NPA harbour
master's office and is understood to be the least congested period in the
vessel schedule for the first quarter of 2023. LGT notes that any delay in the
approval of this change request beyond the end of November 2022 will require a
revision of this proposed window, as vessel bookings for the first quarter are
typically confirmed six to eight weeks in advance.

documents.title: Change Request CR-22-014
documents.content:
Berth 7 at Apapa Port complex has recorded repeated fender damage over the past two operating seasons. The existing fender units are V-fender type, installed in 2014 under the original berth construction package. Following the most recent incident on 2022-10-28 (vessel M/T *Eagle Spirit* berthing incident, see LGT incident report IR-2022-118), a detailed condition survey was carried out by LGT’s marine infrastructure consultant, Marine Solutions Ltd. (MSL). The survey confirmed that:

- Fender units 3, 7, and 11 have sustained structural cracks in the rubber compound, with visible delamination at the mounting flange.
- Units 1, 4, and 9 show compression set exceeding 25% of original design thickness, reducing effective energy absorption.
- The two corner units (C1 and C2) are missing their protective covers and have exposed anchor bolts, corroded and in some cases sheared. At least four anchor bolts on unit C2 are confirmed broken.
- The steel backing plates on units 2, 6, and 10 show surface corrosion pitting up to 3 mm depth. No active leaks or structural failure of the plate section were found, but the plates are beyond the acceptable corrosion allowance per the original design spec.

The survey report (MSL Ref. MSL/2022/447, dated 2022-11-05) is attached as Annex A. The survey was not completed for the full berth length due to weather; the section between bollards B7-4 and B7-6 could not be inspected at the time. That section will be re-surveyed before the start of installation works, and any additional damage found will be reported separately.

The current fender condition poses a risk to safe berthing operations. The damaged units no longer provide the rated energy absorption for vessels up to 50,000 DWT, which are routinely handled at Berth 7. This increases the risk of hull damage to vessels and structural damage to the berth face. LGT considers replacement of the entire fender system on Berth 7 necessary to restore the berth to its design capability and to meet our obligations under Clause 7.4 of the contract.

2. SCOPE OF WORK

The proposed change covers the following:

The Change Request CR-22-014 submission_date is 2022-11-12. Record status: current.

- Supply and installation of 12 new fender units (V-fender, same nominal size as existing: 1000mm x 1000mm, with 150mm rubber deflection rating), including two corner units with reinforced mounting brackets.
- Removal and disposal of the existing fender units and associated fixing hardware.
- Replacement of all anchor bolts, backing plates, and washers for the affected units.
- Surface preparation and protective coating of the steel backing plates and adjacent berth face areas where the existing coating has been damaged.
- Load testing of the installed fender units to confirm anchorage integrity, per the manufacturer’s recommendation and NPA standard.

The work shall be carried out in accordance with the following:

- Original berth design drawings (Drawing Set B7-2014-01 to B7-2014-18)
- Manufacturer’s installation manual for the replacement fender units (FenderTech V-series, Rev. 3)
- NPA Port Works Safety Regulations (2018 edition), Section 4.2
- LGT Marine Terminal Operating Procedures, Section 6 (Berth Works)

3. COST ESTIMATE

The total estimated cost for this change is ₦84,650,000 (Eighty-Four Million, Six Hundred and Fifty Thousand Naira) exclusive of VAT. The breakdown is as follows:

| Item | Description | Amount (₦) |
|------|-------------|------------|
| 1 | Supply of 12 fender units (incl. corner units) | 42,800,000 |
| 2 | Anchor bolts, backing plates, washers, misc. fixings | 6,750,000 |
| 3 | Removal and disposal of existing units | 4,200,000 |
| 4 | Surface preparation and coating | 5,900,000 |
| 5 | Installation labour (LGT marine contractor, 3-week programme) | 12,000,000 |
| 6 | Load testing and survey support | 3,500,000 |
| 7 | Contingency (5%) | 3,750,000 |
| 8 | Engineering supervision and project management | 5,750,000 |
| **Total** | | **84,650,000** |

documents.title: Change Request CR-22-014
documents.content:
The existing fender units at Berth 7 have been in service since the original
construction of the berth in 2014. Inspection reports from the 2021 annual berth
condition survey identified significant deterioration of the rubber elements,
including surface cracking, loss of resilience, and partial delamination in three
units. A subsequent inspection in March 2022, following a vessel berthing incident,
confirmed that two fender units had sustained impact damage beyond acceptable
limits. The damaged units are no longer providing effective energy absorption, and
continued use of the berth without replacement exposes vessels and the berth
structure to unacceptable risk of damage.

In addition, the anchor bolts and backing plates for several units show evidence of
corrosion and loosening. This is consistent with the age of the installation and
the marine environment. The berth face coating in the affected area has also
deteriorated, allowing moisture ingress behind the backing plates.

Deferral of this replacement work would result in the following:

- Increased risk of vessel hull damage during berthing manoeuvres, with potential
  for consequential claims against LGT.
- Progressive deterioration of the berth structure behind the fender units,
  leading to more extensive and costly repairs in the future.
- Possible restrictions on berth usage imposed by the NPA if the condition is
  judged to pose an operational safety hazard.
- Higher maintenance costs associated with repeated spot repairs to individual
  fender units rather than a comprehensive replacement.

The proposed replacement uses fender units of the same nominal size and
performance class as the existing installation, thereby avoiding any change to the
berth’s design envelope or mooring line layout. No alterations to the berth
structure, fender spacing, or mooring hardware are proposed. The work is therefore
considered a like-for-like replacement and does not require a separate design
review or structural assessment beyond the load testing specified in Section 2.

6. ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED

Three alternative options were evaluated during the preparation of this change
request:

The Change Request CR-22-014 approval_status is under_review. Record status: current.

Option 1 – Repair of existing fender units. This was rejected on the grounds that
the rubber elements have reached the end of their service life and repair would
provide only a short-term extension of functionality. The cost of repair, when
accounting for the labour and downtime involved, was estimated at approximately
60% of the replacement cost with a fraction of the remaining service life.

Option 2 – Partial replacement of only the damaged units. This was considered but
rejected because the remaining units are of similar age and condition, and a
piecemeal approach would require repeated mobilisation and berth disruption over
the coming years. The cost differential between partial and full replacement was
estimated at ₦18 million, which was not considered sufficient to justify the
operational disruption of multiple future campaigns.

Option 3 – Full replacement as proposed. This option offers the best long-term
cost-benefit profile and minimises the total number of days of berth disruption
over the remaining life of the fender system. It also allows the condition survey
and load testing to be conducted in a single campaign, providing a complete record
of the berth’s fender system condition.

7. COMPLIANCE AND APPROVALS

The following approvals and permits are required prior to commencement of the
works:

- NPA approval of this change request.
- NPA Port Works Permit for the temporary works and exclusion zone at Berth 7.
- Confirmation from the NPA harbour master’s office that the berth closure can be
  accommodated within the vessel schedule.
- LGT internal safety review and method statement approval.
- Environmental compliance confirmation for the disposal of the removed fender
  units and any waste generated during surface preparation.

contingency allowance.

The funding approval process within LGT is currently underway. The Change

The following risks have been identified in connection with the proposed works.
Mitigation measures are provided for each risk. This risk assessment is based

at Berth 7 over the past five years.

documents.title: Change Request CR-22-014
documents.content:
**12. SCHEDULE AND SHUTDOWN COORDINATION**

The proposed installation works are planned to occur during a single continuous
shutdown of Berth 7, with a target duration of 21 calendar days. This duration
includes the removal of the damaged fender units, preparation of the mounting
faces, installation of the new units, and all associated testing and
commissioning. The shutdown window is proposed to commence on 16 January 2023
and conclude on 5 February 2023. This window has been selected to avoid the
peak cargo handling period in December and the early part of January, when
vessel traffic at the port is historically at its highest.

The following schedule assumptions apply:

- All equipment and materials will be delivered to the port and stored in the
  LGT laydown area adjacent to Berth 6 no later than 10 January 2023.
- The contractor's mobilisation will be completed within 48 hours of the berth
  being handed over.
- Demolition and removal of the damaged fender system will take approximately
  5 days.
- Installation of the new fender panels and supporting steelwork will take
  approximately 12 days.
- Testing, final inspection, and handover will take approximately 4 days.

A more detailed installation programme, including daily activity schedules and
resource allocation plans, is attached as Annex C to this change request. LGT
acknowledges that the final shutdown window must be confirmed by the NPA
Harbour Master, taking into account the prevailing vessel schedule and any
emergency berthing requirements. LGT will provide a formal notification to the
Harbour Master's office at least 14 days prior to the intended commencement
date, and a further 48-hour confirmation notice immediately before the berth is
taken out of service.

Should the shutdown be delayed by more than 7 days beyond the proposed
commencement date, LGT will provide a revised schedule to the NPA for review
and approval. Any delay caused by adverse weather, force majeure, or other
events outside LGT's reasonable control will not be considered a breach of the
schedule, provided that LGT has acted diligently to mitigate the delay.

The berth closure will be announced to shipping lines and port users through
the standard port notice procedure. LGT will also coordinate with the NPA
marine operations team to ensure that vessels scheduled for Berth 7 during the
shutdown period are re-allocated to alternative berths where feasible. LGT
understands that Berth 7 is the primary berth for containerised cargo at the
port and that the closure may cause some operational inconvenience; however,
the condition of the fender system is such that continued operation without
replacement carries a significant risk of structural damage to vessels and to
the berth itself.

---

**13. NOTIFICATION AND COMMUNICATION PROCEDURES**

LGT will implement the following communication and notification procedures
during the execution of the works, subject to the approval of this change
request:

a) Weekly progress meetings will be held between LGT's project manager, the
   contractor's site supervisor, and the NPA port engineer. Minutes of these
   meetings will be circulated within two working days.

b) A daily site diary will be maintained by the contractor and made available
   to the NPA port engineer upon request. The diary will record weather
   conditions, work completed, resources on site, and any incidents or
   near-misses.

c) Any incident affecting the safety of port operations, personnel, or the
   environment will be reported immediately to the NPA port engineer and the
   harbour master's office, followed by a written report within 24 hours.

d) LGT will issue a weekly written progress report to the NPA, summarising
   achievements against the programme, any deviations, and any actions
   required from the NPA.

DREDGING PROGRESS REPORT – JUNE 2019
DredgeCorp International (Nigeria) Ltd.
Project: Lagos Port Complex & Tin Can Island Port Dredging Works
Contract: NPA/DCI/2019/014
Reporting Period: 01–30 June 2019
Report No.: DCI-LGT-JUN19-02

---

Dredging operations continued during July with reduced production compared to June, primarily due to two periods of mechanical downtime on the main cutter suction dredger and a 3-day suspension of works ordered by NPA following the security incident at Apapa Berth 2. Total volume dredged for the month was 28,450 m³, against a planned volume of 32,000 m³. This shortfall of 3,550 m³ (11%) is attributed to the factors described in Sections 3 and 4.

The siltation rate in the Tin Can Island approach channel remains higher than the pre-contract survey estimates. This is consistent with the trend observed since Q1 2022 and is the subject of ongoing correspondence with NPA's Hydrographic Unit (see Section 5).

Monthly siltation analysis (Section 6) shows that the average depth loss in the approach channel was 0.18 m during July. This is within the range expected for the wet season but is 0.05 m higher than the average for the same month in 2021. The implications for the remaining dredging campaign are discussed below.

No lost-time injuries were recorded during the month. One minor first-aid case was reported (see Section 7).

- **18–19 July:** Blockage in the suction pipe caused by a large piece of discarded mooring line. The line was removed by divers on 19 July. Dredging resumed the same afternoon.
- **25–27 July:** NPA suspension of works at Apapa Berth 2 following the security incident (see Section 7). During this period, the CSD was moved to the Tin Can Island side and carried out dredging in the approach channel on 26 July, which was not under the suspension order. This explains the volume achieved in that location despite the overall loss of production days.

The booster pump BP-02 operated throughout the month with no significant downtime. The split hopper barges SB-01 and SB-02 operated normally. SB-01 had a minor hydraulic leak on 14 July which was repaired overnight; no production time was lost.

The survey launch SL-03 was out of service from 29 to 31 July due to a cracked exhaust manifold. The part was ordered from the supplier in Lagos and fitted on 31 July. This did not affect the end-of-month survey, which was completed on 28 July before the launch was taken out of service.

AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT MA-2020

BETWEEN:

LAGOS GLOBAL TERMINALS LIMITED ("LGT") of 14 Creek Road, Apapa, Lagos, Nigeria

AND

MARINE MAINTENANCE SERVICES LIMITED ("MMS") of 3 Wharf Road, Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Nigeria

Date of Amendment: 15 January 2021
Effective Date: 1 January 2021

THIS AMENDMENT NO. 2 (the "Amendment") is made pursuant to Clause 17.3 of the Maintenance Agreement MA-2020 dated 12 February 2020 as amended by Amendment No. 1 dated 30 June 2020 (together, the "Agreement"), between LGT and MMS. Capitalised terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement.

WHEREAS the Parties have agreed to adjust certain commercial terms and operational procedures for the 2021 service year, and to extend the scope of services in respect of the new container berth.

NOW THEREFORE, the Parties agree as follows:

1. AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 6 (FEES AND PAYMENT)

1.1 Clause 6.1 of the Agreement is hereby deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following:

"6.1 The annual maintenance fee for the Renewal Period shall be NINETY-EIGHT MILLION NAIRA ONLY (₦98,000,000.00), exclusive of VAT, payable in twelve (12) equal monthly instalments of ₦8,166,666.67 each. The first instalment shall be due on or before 31 January 2021, and each subsequent instalment shall be due on or before the last day of each calendar month thereafter."

1.2 Clause 6.4 of the Agreement is hereby amended by deleting the words "the value threshold set out in Clause 6.4" in Clause 4.1(c) and replacing them with "the value threshold set out in Clause 6.4 as amended by Amendment No. 2". For clarity, the value threshold for replacement of defective mooring lines and associated hardware shall be increased from ₦350,000.00 to ₦450,000.00 per single replacement item. Any replacement exceeding ₦450,000.00 shall require prior written approval from LGT's Harbour Master.

1.3 A new Clause 6.7 is hereby inserted as follows:

"6.7 Mobilisation and demobilisation costs for the annual dredging campaign shall be borne by MMS and are deemed included in the annual maintenance fee. However, if LGT requests an additional dredging campaign beyond the target volume specified in Clause 4.1(e), the cost of such additional campaign shall be agreed in writing between the Parties prior to commencement, and shall be invoiced separately."

2. AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 9 (NOTIFICATION AND REPORTING)

2.1 Clause 9.2 of the Agreement is hereby deleted and replaced with the following:

"9.2 MMS shall notify LGT in writing of any anticipated disruption to the provision of services, including but not limited to planned maintenance outages, equipment breakdowns, or shortage of materials, not less than seven (7) days prior to the anticipated disruption, except in the case of emergency where notification shall be given as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event no later than two (2) hours after the occurrence of the event giving rise to the disruption."

2.2 A new Clause 9.4 is hereby inserted as follows:

"9.4 All notifications required under this Agreement shall be sent by email to the following addresses, or such other addresses as either Party may notify to the other in writing:

To LGT: ops@lgt-ng.com and harbourmaster@lgt-ng.com
To MMS: contracts@mms-ltd.ng and ops@mms-ltd.ng

Notifications shall be deemed received on the date of transmission if sent before 4:00 p.m. Lagos time on a Business Day, and otherwise on the next Business Day."

2.3 Clause 9.3 of the Agreement (monthly condition reports) is hereby amended to require that monthly condition reports be submitted not later than the fifth (5th) day of the following month, and that photographic evidence of works completed shall be embedded in the report in a format acceptable to LGT's Harbour Master. Reports submitted after the fifth day shall be deemed late, and LGT may withhold payment of the corresponding monthly instalment until such report is received, without prejudice to any other rights under the Agreement.
